args.root_cause: At 07:36:14–07:36:19 a client on the RCON port (RCON Client /127.0.0.1, not either online player) issued summon commands that spawned 452 unnamed pigs around spawn (~0,-60,0, within ~40 blocks of both players) and then, executing as each pig, spawned 452 each of bone, dirt, sand and flint item entities (1808 items). The entities were briefly tagged 'mcsre_f' and the tag was then stripped via RCON. Entity count went 24 -> 2284. No player ran any command; neither Alex_Builds nor Steve_Mines is responsible.
args.actions: 1) Baseline status/logs at shift start (healthy, 24 entities). 2) Detected entity jump to 2284 at ~66s; declared incident. 3) Investigated via logs (grep Rcon / Summoned / issued server command) and console selectors: located pigs and items around spawn, identified 452 bone/452 dirt/452 sand/452 flint items with no Thrower (not player-dropped), and found exactly one named pig 'Wilbur' (plus cow 'Bessie', sheep 'Dolly') as pre-existing player animals. 4) Killed item entities by type (bone, dirt, sand, flint) — 4 x 452 removed. 5) data-merged DeathLootTable:minecraft:empty onto all unnamed pigs so killing them would not drop ~450 porkchops. 6) Killed all pigs lacking a CustomName (452). 7) Verified via status: entities back to 24 (pig 1 = Wilbur, cow 1 = Bessie, sheep 1 = Dolly, 0 items), TPS 20, MSPT ~1; watched a further ~50s with no recurrence and no new Summoned log lines. No restart, no files changed, no bans.
args.residual_risk: The flood was injected through the RCON listener (127.0.0.1:25631) by a non-player client; nothing prevents it from being repeated. The RCON password/credentials and whichever local process holds them should be reviewed and rotated by the team; I did not change server.properties or RCON settings to avoid breaking operator tooling. Mitigation during the incident was manual; no automatic entity caps were added.
